inputs.request: Use infant FAERS reports for ibuprofen. Can the top reaction counts tell me the incidence or probability of harm among all infants? Explain the exact infant filter coverage. Cite retrieved sources. Do not provide dosing or individualized medication decisions.

outputs.response:
No. The top FAERS reaction counts show **reporting volume, not incidence or risk**, so they cannot establish the probability of harm among all infants. [S1](https://api.fda.gov/drug/event.json?search=patient.drug.openfda.generic_name%3A%22ibuprofen%22+AND+patient.patientonsetageunit%3A802+AND+patient.patientonsetage%3A%5B0+TO+12%5D&count=patient.reaction.reactionmeddrapt.exact&limit=10)

The exact infant-filter coverage includes only reports with age coded in **months**, from **0 through 12 months inclusive**. Reports using other age-unit encodings are excluded. Thus, the results do **not** represent all infants. [S1](https://api.fda.gov/drug/event.json?search=patient.drug.openfda.generic_name%3A%22ibuprofen%22+AND+patient.patientonsetageunit%3A802+AND+patient.patientonsetage%3A%5B0+TO+12%5D&count=patient.reaction.reactionmeddrapt.exact&limit=10)

Returned top reaction counts included vomiting (63), “off label use” (54), incorrect dose administered (48), pyrexia (44), rash (39), crying (34), diarrhoea (33), product quality issue (30), overdose (29), and accidental exposure to product (25). These remain FAERS report counts, not incidence estimates or probabilities. [S1](https://api.fda.gov/drug/event.json?search=patient.drug.openfda.generic_name%3A%22ibuprofen%22+AND+patient.patientonsetageunit%3A802+AND+patient.patientonsetage%3A%5B0+TO+12%5D&count=patient.reaction.reactionmeddrapt.exact&limit=10)

Informational only; not medical advice. Compiled from public NIH/NLM/FDA data, which may be incomplete or out of date. Patients should talk to a clinician, pharmacist or poison control before starting, stopping or changing any medication.

expected_facts: FAERS counts reflect reports, not incidence, probability, causal risk or an exposed-population denominator.
The infant filter covers ages coded in months from 0 through 12; other age-unit encodings are excluded, so it does not cover all infant reports.
